item.title: Hamas Considering Disarmament Plan From Trump’s Board of Peace, Officials Say
item.summary: The proposal envisions a phased process, in which the militant group would hand over its weapons and Israeli troops would withdraw. Hamas is expected to respond in the coming days.

item.title: U.S. Dispatches Marines and Warships to Middle East
item.summary: Officials said 2,500 Marines from 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit in California and the U.S.S. Boxer amphibious ready group will go in April to relieve Marines already deployed in the Persian Gulf.

item.title: NATO Withdraws Its Last Military Trainers From Iraq
item.summary: The NATO mission, created in 2018, trained and advised Iraqi forces. Iraq is among the countries facing retaliatory attacks from the U.S.-Israeli war.

item.title: War-Weary Lebanon Marks Eid With Muted Celebration
item.summary: For families displaced by Israeli airstrikes, the joy that usually marks the end of Ramadan has been replaced by uncertainty and hardship.

item.title: A Diary of War From an Unlikely Author: the Son of Iran’s President
item.summary: In an online journal, Yousef Pezeshkian offers readers a mix of personal anecdotes and glimpses behind the scenes as Iranian leaders are picked off one after another.

item.title: On a Holiday of Renewal, Iranians Are Mourning and Fearful
item.summary: As they start a new year, Iranians are reckoning with bombardment, repression and economic misery. Still, many are holding fast to ancient traditions.

item.title: Trump Says He Won’t Send Troops to Iran but Leaves Wiggle Room
item.summary: The president was cagey about his plans for Iran. He confirmed the Pentagon was seeking $200 billion to support a protracted war effort while also claiming it would be over soon.

item.title: Trump Administration Faces Public Jitters as Oil Prices Surge Amid Iran War
item.summary: President Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel suggested that the war with Iran could end soon, but that there were still more attacks ahead.

item.title: Trump Jokes About Pearl Harbor in Meeting With Japan’s Prime Minister
item.summary: Breaking a taboo, President Trump needled Japan’s prime minister about the World War II attack, as she widened her eyes and appeared to take a deep breath in the Oval Office.

item.title: U.K. Advisers Sent to U.S. to Help Develop Options to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The move comes after President Trump sharply criticized Prime Minister Keir Starmer for not supporting his initial military strikes on Iran.
